title: Absolute Pin on the Knight
description: White's bishop on g5 pins the f6 knight to the queen on d8. Black's d5 pawn is attacked three times but defended only by that pinned knight. Win material.
hints: Count the attackers and defenders of the d5 pawn
Can the f6 knight really recapture on d5?
explanation: d5 is attacked by the e4 pawn, the c3 knight and the c4 bishop, and defended only by the f6 knight. That knight is pinned: if it ever recaptures on d5, Bxd8 wins the queen. So White simply wins a clean pawn. Nxd5 is the most active capture, adding a second attacker to the pinned knight.
followUp: After 1.Nxd5 Black usually breaks the pin with ...Be7, and White stays a healthy pawn up.

title: Back-Rank Weakness
description: Black's king is boxed in by its own pawns on f7, g7 and h7, with no escape square. White has a rook on a1. Find the winning move.
hints: Black's king cannot move — it is trapped by its own pawns
Which file leads directly to the black king?
explanation: Ra8# is checkmate! The rook slides to the 8th rank where Black's king has no escape. This is the classic back-rank mate — always ensure your king has a flight square.
followUp: Preventive measure: always move one of g7/h7/f7 a square forward to give the king an escape.

title: Knight Fork Opportunity
description: Black's queen on f4 has strayed into dangerous territory. White's knight can execute a deadly fork. Find it!
hints: Which White piece can attack two valuable Black pieces simultaneously?
Think about the knight on f3 — where can it go to attack king and queen?
explanation: Nd5! forks the queen on f4 and threatens Nc7+ forking the king and rook. Black cannot save both. This shows how an over-eager queen can become a target.

title: Exploiting the Open d-File
description: Black has a strong central presence with pawns on d5 and e5. How should Black exploit the position? Think about pawn breaks and piece activity.
hints: Black's pawns control the centre — advance one to challenge White
Which White piece is the most passive? Can you challenge it?
explanation: d4! gains central space, limits the White Nc3, and opens lines for Black's pieces. After Ne2 Bc5, Black has excellent piece activity and a strong centre. The principle: advance your central pawns when you have the chance.

title: Minority Attack Preparation
description: This is a Queen's Gambit Declined structure. White has the minority attack plan with b4-b5. Find the first step.
hints: White has two queenside pawns vs Black's three. This is the minority — push it!
The plan is b4-b5xc6, creating a weakness on c6 or d5
explanation: b4! starts the minority attack. White will play b5 next, forcing ...bxc5 or ...cxb5. Either way, Black gets a weak pawn. This is a classic positional weapon in Queen's Gambit positions.
followUp: After b5 cxb5 Nxb5, White has excellent piece activity and Black's queenside is weak.

title: Bishop Pair Advantage
description: White has the bishop pair. The position is semi-open — ideal for bishops. How can White activate the bishop pair most effectively?
hints: Trade a knight for a bishop to give your opponent the bishop pair? No — keep yours!
Open the position for your bishops with a pawn advance
explanation: Nf3 develops a piece with tempo, readying O-O and d4. In open positions, bishop pairs are powerful — the plan is to open the position with d4, creating diagonals for both bishops. Don't rush to trade them!

title: Pawn Break to Open Lines
description: Black has the bishop pair and pieces ready. Find the pawn break that opens the position for the bishops.
hints: You have two powerful bishops — they need open diagonals to operate
Look for a central pawn advance that challenges White's structure
explanation: d4! grabs central space and opens the a6-f1 diagonal for the dark-squared bishop. After Nb1 e5 or Nb5 Bf6, Black's bishops become dominant. The principle: use pawn advances to activate your bishops.

title: Discovered Attack
description: White's pieces are lined up for a discovered attack. Moving one piece will unveil a devastating threat from the piece behind it.
hints: Look at which White pieces are aligned with Black's king or queen on a diagonal or file
Moving which White piece would reveal an attack by the piece behind it?
explanation: Ng5! threatens Nxf7 (fork: king + rook) and simultaneously uncovers the Bc4 bearing down on f7. The double threat is too much: if 1...h6 2.Nxf7 Rxf7 3.Bxf7+ Kxf7 wins material.

title: Deflection Tactic
description: Black can use a deflection tactic to win material. A key White piece is overloaded — force it away from its defensive duty.
hints: What piece is defending an important square for White?
Can you attack that defender in a way that forces it to move, abandoning its duty?
explanation: Ng4! attacks the Bc4 and simultaneously threatens Nxf2 forking king and rook. White's knight on f3 is the only defender of f2 — if it moves (to defend the bishop), Nxf2 wins. This is a deflection/overload combo.
followUp: After 1...Ng4 2.Bxf7+ Kxf7 3.Ne5+ Ke6 4.Nxd7 Nxd7 the position is complicated but Black has compensation.

title: Isolated Queen's Pawn
description: Black has an isolated pawn on e4. White should blockade it and convert the long-term weakness. What is the right strategic plan?
hints: An isolated pawn can only be defended by pieces, not pawns — this is its weakness
Place a piece in front of the isolated pawn to blockade it permanently
explanation: Ne5! blockades the isolated e4 pawn on the ideal square. The knight on e5 is powerful, cannot be dislodged, and attacks c6. White will then target the e4 pawn with Re1 and other pieces. The principle: blockade weaknesses with knights.
followUp: After Ne5 Nxe5 Rxe5, the isolated pawn is fixed and White will win it in the long run.

title: Exchange Sacrifice for Attack
description: White can sacrifice the exchange for a powerful attack against Black's king. Find the right continuation.
hints: Material isn't everything — initiative and attack can be worth more than a rook
Look for a sacrifice on d6 or c6 to open lines against the Black king
explanation: Nd5! is a positional pawn sacrifice. After Nd5 Nxd5 exd5, White has the powerful d5 pawn cramp and open e-file. If Nd5 Qxd5 Qxd5 Nxd5 Bb5, White wins material. The knight dominates d5 outpost.
followUp: White's plan: Nd5, f4-f5, g4 kingside attack. Black lacks counterplay.

title: Prophylaxis — Stop the Threat
description: Black is threatening ...e5 to activate the bishop on d6 and gain central space. White must prevent this with prophylaxis. Find the best preventive move.
hints: Think like Nimzowitsch: 'First restrain, then blockade, then destroy'
Which move prevents ...e5 while also being useful developmentally?
explanation: e4! anticipates and prevents ...e5 by claiming the e4 square first. After dxe4 Nxe4 Nxe4 Bxe4, White has the bishop pair and central control. Prophylaxis means preventing your opponent's plans before they can execute them.
followUp: White plans Bc2, Qd3, 0-0 with easy play. Black's bishop on d6 is no longer active.
